$comment: Probes that fail TODAY, where, how, and the pull request that fixes each (verdict.mjs). The list may only shrink: a listed probe that passes turns its cell red, so the fixing pull request deletes its entry. `when` maps an axis to a value or a list; an entry without `when` matches every run. `failure` is a regex for the expected failure, the bug itself; `consequences` (optional) matches lines the bug causes but that do not identify it, accepted only beside a `failure` match. Every failure line must be accounted for, so a crash, a TypeError or a lost file in a listed probe is still a REGRESSION, and an applying entry whose `failure` matches no line is STALE (verdict.mjs). Entries and signatures were derived from local runs on Vitest 5 and 4.1.11 (RNTL 12.9, 13.3 and 14.1, both engines, every runtime combination; the isolated layout as a pnpm-shaped store built by run.mjs --link-deps) except where `why` says otherwise.

entries.failure: ^rntl-auto-cleanup\.test\.tsx: the previous test's tree was unmounted: AssertionError: expected \+0 to be 1
entries.why: RNTL registers cleanup only through a global afterEach. Both engines, every RNTL.

entries.failure: ^rntl-findby-fake-timers\.test\.tsx: findBy advances Vitest's fake timers: Error: Unable to find an element with text: ready
entries.why: RNTL drives fake timers only through a global jest, which only jest-compat defines. Both engines, every RNTL, globals on or off. NOTE: #342 documents this as a limitation (use jest-compat, or advance timers by hand) and does not fix it, so this entry will not go stale when #342 merges; no open pull request fixes it.

entries.failure: ^rntl-nested-text\.test\.tsx: nested Text is queryable by its own text: Error: Unable to find an element with text: inner
entries.why: RCTVirtualText is registered as a text host for RNTL 14 only.

entries.failure: ^unhandled error \(from recoverable-error\.test\.tsx\): Error: There was an error during concurrent rendering but React was able to recover by instead synchronously rendering the entire root\.
entries.consequences: ^the JSON report says success: true, but Vitest exited 1$
entries.why: react-test-renderer 19 reports a recoverable error through process.emit('uncaughtException'). RNTL 14 renders without it. Both engines.
A synchronous requireActual compiles a second module graph under Node, so the mock's real `read` sees Node's store.

entries.failure: ^partial-mock-store\.test\.ts: \[vitest\] There was an error when mocking a module\..* \(caused by: Error: Cannot find module '[^']*/src/partial-mock/store' imported from [^)]*/src/partial-mock/api\.ts\)$
entries.why: Under the mock engine the synchronous jest.requireActual reaches Node's ESM loader, which cannot resolve api.ts's extensionless import of ./store, so the factory throws: 'Cannot find module …/src/partial-mock/store imported from …/api.ts'. Vitest reports only that mocking failed, and the JSON report drops the cause, so the signature is on the cause the accounting reporter records. #345 rewrites requireActual in the factory to vi.importActual for both engines, but that it clears this symptom is NOT yet observed.

entries.failure: ^aliased-sibling-string\.test\.ts: .*: AssertionError: expected null to be 'written by the test'
entries.why: The sibling's directory is externalized, so Node loads the aliased source and its own store. Observed to pass with jest-compat on, whose Node-side resolution reaches the same copy.
Node's alias fallback cannot represent a regex alias: Cannot find module.
Node compiles the aliased source to CommonJS: Cannot use 'import.meta' outside a module.

entries.failure: ^esm-default-interop\.test\.ts: .*: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined \(reading '__extends'\)
entries.why: Babel's interopRequireDefault reads exports.default from __esModule CommonJS.

entries.failure: ^jest-fake-timer-options\.test\.ts: .*: AssertionError: expected 'the fake clock stood still' to be 'fired'
entries.why: jest.useFakeTimers passes Jest's options to Vitest, which drops advanceTimers. Both engines.

entries.failure: ^jest-error-equality\.test\.ts: .*: AssertionError: expected Error: bad input .* to deeply equal Error: bad input
entries.why: Vitest compares Errors' own enumerable properties, per-instance methods included. Both engines.

entries.failure: ^the banner does not name the safeAreaContext preset: \[vitest-native\] engine: (native|mock)
entries.why: The banner names no presets. Both engines.

entries.failure: ^hot-automock-[ab]\.test\.ts: gets its own factory, and an automock for the module it automocks: AssertionError: expected false to be true
entries.why: Vitest 4.1 replays a remembered factory from a placeholder node the hot runtime keeps across files; Vitest 5 is unaffected (the probe is n/a there). Observed locally on Vitest 4.1.11 (a copy linked with run.mjs --link-deps), matching #338's own reproduction.

entries.failure: ^unhandled error: VitestNativeError: \[vitest-native\] hotRuntime state restoration failed: / - react-native\.appearance restore: Cannot read properties of null \(reading 'setColorScheme'\)$
entries.consequences: ^(hot-rn-module-mock-[ab]\.test\.ts: did not run|file accounting: (no result in the JSON report for|Vitest never reported module) hot-rn-module-mock-[ab]\.test\.ts|the JSON report says success: true, but Vitest exited 1)$
entries.why: The per-file reset restores React Native before it clears jest-compat's Node mock registry, so the Appearance restore reads the null mock and throws outside Vitest's per-file error handling: the second file is never collected, and the JSON report says success: true while Vitest exits 1. The pair is symmetric, so either file may be the lost one; both lost is a REGRESSION (verdict.mjs: a consequence cannot account for every file of the probe).

worklets' Jest resolver drops .native for any directory whose path contains its name, and pnpm names the library's store directory after its worklets peer. Observed locally in a pnpm-shaped store (run.mjs --link-deps); not yet in a real pnpm install.

The same substring check matches reanimated's own store directory (named after its worklets peer), so all of reanimated resolves its web files, which import react-native-web. Observed locally in a pnpm-shaped store; not yet in a real pnpm install.
